resale_co.name: Resale Certificate of Property Compliance (CPC)
resale_co.issued_by: Department of Housing, Code Enforcement & Rent Leveling (Code Enforcement Office)
resale_co.lead_time: The fee depends on how early the request is received: more than 10 business days before closing for the lowest fee. Request the inspection before the date of sale.
requirements: Inspection under the 2015 International Property Maintenance Code (the City's checklist is a general guide, not a full list)
Clean yard, grass and weeds under 10 inches, no rat infestation, sound accessory structures
House number at least 4 inches high
Sound foundation, walls, roof, gutters, chimney, porches, stairs and decks
Windows and doors in good repair and weather tight; screens from April 15 to October 15
Interior surfaces sanitary with no peeling or loose paint or plaster; railings and guards where required
Working plumbing with no leaks; water heater installed right with relief valve and discharge pipe
Heat of at least 65 degrees from October 1 to May 15; fuel-burning appliances vented outside
At least 60 amp electric service, 2 outlets per habitable room, GFCI outlet in bathroom and laundry, cover plates on all outlets
Exit doors and windows openable from inside without keys (no double-keyed deadbolts)
One fire extinguisher within 10 feet of the kitchen (on the 2021 checklist)
Smoke detectors on every level, in every bedroom and in the hall outside sleeping areas; CO detectors within 10 feet of all bedrooms

fees.label: Resale Certificate of Property Compliance / inspection, request received more than 10 business days before closing (City Code 149-20A(1))
fees.quote: Requests for a certificate of property compliance/inspection received more than 10 business days prior to the closing date: $35.

fees.label: Request received 4 to 10 business days before closing (City Code 149-20A(2))
fees.quote: Requests for a certificate of property compliance/inspection received four to 10 business days prior to the closing date: $70.

fees.label: Request received fewer than 4 business days before closing (City Code 149-20A(3))
fees.quote: Requests for a certificate of property compliance/inspection received fewer than four business days prior to the closing date: $125.

fees.label: Each additional re-inspection (one re-inspection is included in the base fee)
fees.quote: One reinspection is included in the base fee. Each additional reinspection: $40.

resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Certificate of Property Compliance (check 'Seller' and 'SALE APPLICATION', give the buyer and agent details) and file it with the Code Enforcement Office, City Hall, 181 E Commerce Street, Bridgeton, NJ 08302. Call 856-455-3230 (Housing Supervisor ext. 223, Housing Office Clerk ext. 217) to confirm the fee and schedule the inspection.

evidence.quote: Resale Certificates Upon the sale of any property within the City of Bridgeton, a resale CPC needs to be filled out and filed with the Code Enforcement Office.
the Code Enforcement Office also handles the registration of rental units, home sales, vacant or abandoned property, and follow-up on property maintenance complaints.

No owner or agent thereof shall hereafter sell or convey, whether legal or equitable title, any dwelling or dwelling unit, or premises, except vacant land, unless prior to such sale or conveyance a certificate of inspection/certificate of property compliance has been obtained from the Code Enforcement Officer.
The owner, buyer, or agent shall request an inspection prior to the date of sale and shall ensure that the dwelling is accessible for the inspection.

If, at the time of inspection, the property does not meet all the requirements necessary to obtain a certificate of property compliance and the dwelling unit is unoccupied, a certificate of inspection may be issued in lieu of the certificate of property compliance if applicable provisions for the certificate of inspection have been satisfied.
Residential property sales and residential rental property sales certificate of inspection or certificate of property compliance fee under §265-32 shall be as follows:
The per inspection fee for an initial inspection of a rental unit to obtain a Certificate of Property Compliance shall be $35.

resale_co.notes: City Code Chapter 265, Article V (Sale of Residential Property, 265-32) says no dwelling may be sold or conveyed unless a certificate of inspection or certificate of property compliance has first been obtained from the Code Enforcement Officer, and after a sale no one may occupy the home without a certificate of property compliance. If an unoccupied home fails, a certificate of inspection may be issued instead. Resale fees are in City Code 149-20A, tiered by business days before closing ($35 / $70 / $125, one re-inspection included, $40 for each extra re-inspection). The code text (Chapters 149 and 265) was read in full through the ecode360 print view. The Housing page note 'Effective July 14th, 2025 ... First Inspection $35, Re-inspections $18' matches City Code 149-20F, which covers rental units only (Ord. 25-10, June 17, 2025), so it is not used as the resale fee. Under 265-32C, real estate agents are treated as the owner's agent and can be charged if the certificate is not obtained. The CPC application's second page describes the State lead-safe inspection law (P.L.2021, c.182) for rental units; that is a rental requirement. Rental registration ($45 per year by March 1, $75 after) is a rental program. City Code 149-34 also lists 'certificate of property compliance' fees ($120 per residential unit) in the Uniform Construction Code fee schedule; those are construction certificates, not the resale CPC.

requirements: Smoke alarms (UL listed) on every level; battery-only alarms must be the 10-year sealed battery type, and hardwired alarms cannot be replaced with battery alarms
Basement smoke alarm at the bottom of the stairwell, on the ceiling (not between joists)
A 10-year sealed smoke alarm in every bedroom
Smoke alarms and CO alarms must be less than 10 years old and working
Carbon monoxide alarm in the hallway within 10 feet of all bedrooms
House numbers at least 4 inches high, contrasting color, permanently fixed and visible from the street
Homes with solar panels, a backup generator or battery storage need a permanent printed 'Caution: Multiple Sources of Power' label at the main electrical panel and the electric meter
If there is a fire alarm system, a report from the alarm company is required (per the online application form)

authorities.how_to_apply: Fill out the online 'CO and Smoke Certification Application' (Google Form) linked from the Bridgeton Fire Department's Uniform Fire Code page, picking Bridgeton City as the municipality. Payment is due at the time of the inspection by check or money order payable to the City of Bridgeton Fire Department (the form says an online payment link will be on the invoice). Re-inspection for a failed or no-show inspection costs the same as the first inspection. The certificate is emailed to the address given and is valid for 90 days. Questions: firedepartment@cityofbridgeton.com or 856-451-0090 / 856-451-0091.

fire_cert.notes: The City of Bridgeton Fire Department (registry code F) is the local fire enforcing agency and issues the resale smoke/CO certificate through its Bureau of Fire Prevention at 1 Orange Street. Fees, lead time and the 90-day validity come from the Bureau's 'Occupancy & Smoke Certificates' guideline sheet (created November 20, 2025) and match the online application form. The guideline sheet does not list a fire extinguisher (in line with P.L.2025, c.19) but does require 10-year sealed battery alarms and the secondary power source label. The middle fee tier is printed as '7 business days prior'; the gap between 4 and 10 days is not spelled out. Jack Justice Jr.'s email (justicej@cityofbridgeton.com) is linked from his name on the Department page and printed in the state fire directory; the Bureau's general address is firedepartment@cityofbridgeton.com. City Code 149-15A also lists a $30 annual fire registration fee for 'R-A non-owner-occupied 1 and 2 units', which is inspected and charged only upon sale or change of tenant; this applies to non-owner-occupied (rental) homes and is separate from the smoke/CO certificate.

other_items.label: Final water meter reading
other_items.detail: The City charges for a final meter reading by how early it is requested: $35 more than 10 business days before closing, $70 for 4 to 10 business days, $125 for fewer than 4 business days (City Code 149-35H). The fee is paid with the final water bill.
